text:
Oliver Bjorkstrand plays under 12 minutes a night for the Rangers and has seven goals, the same as Tye Kartye and Gabe Perreault in far less ice time. At 31, on his fourth team, he's found a role that fits: third-line minutes, some power-play work, and shots from good places.

The scoring rate, 2.68 points per 60, is well above his recent seasons, and some of that is running ahead of the chances: 7 goals on 4.5 expected. But his own shot quality is also up, 1.11 expected goals per 60 against 0.86 last season, so this isn't all luck. Our talent range, which leans on his history, sees about 20 goals over the full season.

The bigger change is defensive. Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 10% of forwards for creating offense last season, but this year the Rangers take 55% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on ice, a bit better than without him. Our model compares him to Victor Olofsson, another scoring winger finding a second life in a smaller role. For a team that leans on its top six, a third-liner who scores is a quiet edge.
